messages:
From: Evan Moore <evan.moore@saffronrms.com>

Cc: Saffron RMS Infra <infra@saffronrms.com>

Subject: Sudden p95/503 spikes on our private VPC after last canary

Kim,

We started seeing a ~3x p95 latency jump and intermittent 503/429s for inference traffic to the private cluster around 06:30 PDT after your team’s canary roll. The pattern is noisy: spikes last 5–10 minutes, then fall back, and repeat. This is impacting our critical SLAs for downstream scoring.

I attached a short log capture and a CSV with the service-level metrics for the last 4 hours. Key details:
- Model variant: redwood-v3-quant (pinned before the canary) vs redwood-v3-ff (canary)
- Traffic: ~400 QPS, median seq len 120 tokens
- Errors: 503s with message: "model overloaded" and 429s on some routes

Can your on-call ops help investigate? We need a mitigation path ASAP — we’re prepared to cut traffic to hosted fallback or roll back the canary. Our execs are asking for a status update within the hour.

Thanks,
Evan Moore
Head of Platform, Saffron RMS

Attachments: saffron_hotpath_sample.log (text), svc-metrics-20260509.csv (csv)

Evan — thanks for the quick heads up and the artifacts. I’ve pulled Marcus (serving runtime), Laura (private deployment lead), Marissa (CS), and Tessa (SRE) into this thread. We’ll treat this as an urgent hotpath incident.

Immediate plan (short):
- Marcus + SRE will validate kernel/quant path selection and batch sizing for the canary variant.
- If we confirm a regression, we’ll either (A) pin traffic back to the previous model variant, or (B) switch routing to hosted fallback for the affected routes.
- We’ll collect: per-shard memory/KV cache metrics, GPU utilization profiles, and grpc/frontend queue lengths.

Can you confirm whether you want us to proceed with a rollback if we see continued 503s, or do you prefer we first attempt a traffic funnel to hosted fallback for specific endpoints? Also confirm maintenance windows — if we need a short rolling restart to reclaim KV fragments that Saffron saw previously, we need a 20–30 minute window.

I’ll update your execs in an hour with preliminary findings.

—Kimberly

Marking current observations + quick triage notes.

Observations from a first-pass on the provided logs:
- 503s correlate with busy periods on a subset of shards (shard ids 3,7). GPU util on those nodes jumps to 98–100% right before 503 bursts.
- There are repeated KV cache misses on long prefixes (seq length >100) which triggers heavier attention to attention and longer decode times.
- The canary variant (redwood-v3-ff) uses a slightly different kernel path that increases register pressure for our quantized kernels; under sustained >80% GPU that appears to cascade into GC-like stalls.

Immediate mitigations to try (ordered by invasiveness):
1) Can we pin affected routes to the previous variant (redwood-v3-quant) for 1 hour? That’s the fastest way to drop p95 while we dig in.
2) If rollback not acceptable, enable conservative batching knobs (max_batch_tokens lower bound) and reduce per-batch token cap to avoid building huge batches during spikes.
3) If we still see noisy 503s, schedule a 30m rolling restart on the 2 hot shards to clear potential KV fragmentation; Tessa can coordinate.

I’m standing by to perform a controlled pin and to push a config patch; Kim, give the go for rollback and I’ll execute immediately.

—Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Evan — we rolled the traffic back to redwood-v3-quant for the impacted endpoints at 08:35 PDT. Early telemetry shows p95 dropped ~55% and 503s subsided on the hot shards. Marcus and Tessa will continue a focused investigation into the kernel path and batching behavior that exposed the regression; we will:

- Run a reproducer against the canary variant in a scaled test cluster to validate register pressure and KV miss patterns.
- Tune batch size heuristics and add a temporary cap on max_batch_tokens for private deployments until we ship a permanent kernel/regression fix.
- Provide a technical postmortem plus an action checklist within 48 hours.

Action items for Saffron: please share any longer log windows and confirm whether you want us to schedule a 30-minute rolling restart later tonight (we recommend a midnight window to minimize user impact).

I’m elevating this to execs for awareness (copied). If you’d like a short call with my team and your VP of Engineering, we can schedule within the next two hours.

—Kimberly Park
